sentences.text: Ian Marcel Craig Garcia has served as chief executive officer of Coca-Cola FEMSA, the Mexico City-based Coca-Cola bottler listed as KOF, since 2023.

sentences.quote: Joined FEMSA in 1994 and Coca-Cola FEMSA in 2003 and was appointed as CEO in 2023. He is also the President of the company's Sustainability Committee.

sentences.quote: Coca-Cola FEMSA's Board of Directors has appointed Ian Craig Garcia, currently CEO of Coca-Cola FEMSA Brazil, to become Coca-Cola FEMSA's Chief Executive Officer as of the same date.
sentences.text: His appointment, announced in October 2022, saw him succeed John Santa Maria after leading Coca-Cola FEMSA Brazil from 2016.

sentences.quote: Ian serves on the Board of Directors of Republic Services, Inc., a leader in the environmental services industry.
sentences.text: He also sits on the board of Republic Services.

mgmt_bio.text: He joined FEMSA in 1994 and Coca-Cola FEMSA in 2003, and he also presides over the company's Sustainability Committee. Across more than two decades in the beverage industry he held senior roles including chief operating officer of Brazil, chief operating officer of Argentina, CFO and strategic planning director of the South America division, CFO and planning and corporate affairs director for the Mercosur region, and corporate finance and treasury director. His appointment, announced in October 2022, saw him succeed John Santa Maria after leading Coca-Cola FEMSA Brazil from 2016. He also sits on the board of Republic Services.

sentences.text: Coca-Cola FEMSA named Pamela Ortiz Investor Relations Director effective August 1, 2026, succeeding Jorge Collazo, IR Director since 2022, who became Strategic Planning Director for Coca-Cola FEMSA Brazil.
At board level, Jennifer K. Mann resigned as a Series D director on June 12, 2026 and was replaced the same day by Sedef Salingan Sahin, Coca-Cola's chief digital officer.

Craig said the company is focused on adapting to the evolving consumer environment, accelerating digital transformation and leveraging revenue growth management, expecting Mexico's consumer environment to stay subdued.

thesis_pillars.text: Coca-Cola FEMSA is the largest Coca-Cola franchise bottler in the world by sales volume, reaching more than 2.2 million points of sale and over 276 million consumers in Latin America. Geographic diversification cushions single-market weakness: in the second quarter of 2026 Colombia, Guatemala and Brazil posted record volumes while Mexico faced a difficult consumer environment and an excise tax increase. Input costs and pricing are supporting profitability, with gross margin expanding 180 basis points to 47.1% on favorable sweetener and PET costs and operating income up 9.1%. Capital discipline is improving, as FEMSA cited lower capital expenditure at Coca-Cola FEMSA from a more selective approach to capital deployment.
